findings.title: deleteCache mutation never invalidates the connectedCalendars query, leaving stale cache status on screen
findings.body: The deleteCache mutation's onSuccess only shows a toast and calls the optional onSuccess prop (onChanged). Unlike the disconnect mutation right below it (which explicitly invalidates viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars and viewer.apps.integrations in onSettled), nothing refetches connectedCalendars after a cache delete. The cacheUpdatedAt value that drives the 'Cache Status' display and the 'Delete cached data' menu item comes from that query, so after a successful deletion the UI will continue to show the old cache timestamp and offer deletion again until something else triggers a refetch — and in usages where onChanged is not provided it never updates. Add utils.viewer.calendars.connectedCalendars.invalidate() to the deleteCache mutation's onSettled.

findings.title: getCacheStatusByCredentialIds counts expired cache rows as active cache
findings.body: The new groupBy query aggregates over all CalendarCache rows for the given credentials with no expiresAt filter. Everywhere else the cache is read (getCachedAvailability) rows are only served when expiresAt >= now, so an expired row is functionally dead. But connectedCalendars.handler uses this method to compute cacheUpdatedAt, which the UI uses to decide whether to show 'Cache Status: Last updated ...' and the 'Delete cached data' action. A credential whose only cache rows expired weeks ago will still be presented as having an active cache with a misleading 'last updated' timestamp. The where clause should include expiresAt: { gte: new Date() } to match the read path semantics.

findings.title: Handler throws a generic Error, surfacing as HTTP 500 instead of a proper tRPC error code
findings.body: When the credential does not exist or belongs to another user, the handler throws `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")`. In tRPC a plain Error is converted into an INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500) response, which misleads clients and error monitoring into treating an expected authorization/not-found case as a server crash. The rest of the codebase uses TRPCError with code "NOT_FOUND" or "FORBIDDEN" for these cases; this should too.

findings.title: dev:cron now uses npx tsx but tsx is not a declared dependency
findings.body: The script was changed from `ts-node cron-tester.ts` to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts`, but tsx does not appear in dependencies or devDependencies of this package (ts-node is still declared). `npx tsx` will fetch an unpinned tsx version from the registry on each fresh machine, which fails in offline/restricted environments, is non-deterministic across developers, and can break under yarn 3 PnP setups. Add tsx as a pinned devDependency and invoke it via yarn, or keep ts-node.

findings.title: Script uses macOS-only sed syntax and a CWD-relative .env path
findings.body: `sed -i '' -E ...` is the BSD/macOS form of in-place edit; on GNU sed (Linux, including CI containers and most dev VMs) the empty string is interpreted as a file name and the command errors out, so the script silently fails to update GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL for Linux users. Additionally ENV_FILE="../.env" only resolves correctly if the script happens to be invoked from inside the scripts/ directory; running it from the repo root creates/updates a .env one level above the repository. Use a portable sed invocation (e.g. `sed -i.bak` plus cleanup, or detect GNU vs BSD) and resolve ENV_FILE relative to the script's own location.

findings.title: Cache timestamp is hardcoded to en-US formatting regardless of the user's locale
findings.body: The 'Last updated' timestamp is formatted with `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)`, so every user — including those with a different app locale and different date conventions (day/month ordering, 24h clock) — sees a US-formatted date. The formatter should use the user's locale (available via useLocale / i18n.language) or the browser default by omitting the locale argument.

findings.title: No tests for the new deleteCache mutation's ownership check or the cache-status repository method
findings.body: This PR adds a destructive, user-facing mutation (deleteCache) whose only protection is the userId ownership check in the handler, plus a new repository aggregation (getCacheStatusByCredentialIds) that drives what the UI displays. Neither has any test coverage: there is no test that a user cannot delete another user's credential cache (the security-critical path), nor any test covering the groupBy/mapping behavior. Given this is a security-sensitive destructive endpoint, at minimum the authorization failure case and the happy path should be covered.
